findings.evidence: grep: `HungerbuhlerWasem.lean:105:    (hγ_imm : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b)`; `PiecewiseC1On.lean:33: Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b — γ is continuous on [[a,b]] and C¹ on every closed subinterval whose interior avoids a fixed finite breakpoint set`. Reparam.lean:71-72 require pointwise `DifferentiableAt` and continuity of `deriv γ` on all of `φ '' [[c,d]]`.
findings.fix: State the invariance at the piecewise-C¹ level: take `IsPiecewiseC1On γ` on the image (or `IsPwC1ImmersionOn`) and use Mathlib's `intervalIntegral.integral_deriv_smul_comp'''`, which needs only `HasDerivWithinAt` on the open interval plus integrability, splitting `[[c,d]]` at the preimages of the finitely many breakpoints (monotone φ suffices for the basepoint-shift case). At minimum add a monotone/affine pwC¹ corollary so the cited basepoint use is actually reachable, and record the C¹-only restriction in the module docstring, which currently does not mention it.
findings.issue: `hγ : ∀ u ∈ φ '' [[c,d]], DifferentiableAt ℝ γ u` together with `hγ' : ContinuousOn (deriv γ) (φ '' [[c,d]])` forces γ to be C¹ with no breakpoints. The library's ambient curve class is piecewise C¹: `hungerbuhlerWasem_residueTheorem` takes `IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b` (HungerbuhlerWasem.lean:105) and `IsPiecewiseC1On` is the roadmap's regularity predicate (PiecewiseC1On.lean). The PR description cites the summit's basepoint residual as the motivation, but no closed pwC¹ contour (rectangle, polygon, concatenation) satisfies these hypotheses, so the API cannot discharge it. Same over-strong regularity in `IsNullHomologous.comp_reparam` (line 129) and, via `himg`, in `windingNumber_comp_reparam_affine` (line 113).

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/Deriv/Comp.lean:149: `theorem deriv.scomp (hg : DifferentiableAt 𝕜' g₁ (h x)) (hh : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 h x) : deriv (g₁ ∘ h) x = deriv h x • deriv g₁ (h x)`.
findings.fix: Generalize `γ` to `ℝ → E` for `[NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]` — the proof `(hγ.hasDerivAt.scomp t hφ).deriv` is unchanged — or drop the lemma and use `hφ.deriv ▸ deriv.scomp` at the one call site.
findings.issue: `deriv_comp_reparam` is pure calculus with nothing complex-analytic in it, but is stated only for `γ : ℝ → ℂ`. Mathlib's `deriv.scomp` proves the same identity for arbitrary `𝕜`, `𝕜'` and normed space `E`; the TauCeti version is a strictly less general restatement, differing only by naming the speed via `HasDerivAt φ (φ' t) t` instead of `deriv φ t`. `eqOn_deriv_comp_reparam` (line 77) inherits the same restriction.

summary: The reparametrization API is stated for C¹ curves, one level above the piecewise-C¹ class that the roadmap's curve layer and the summit theorem actually use, so it cannot serve the basepoint use it cites; and the chain-rule helper is a ℂ-specialization of a general Mathlib lemma.
